\chapter{Evening}
\label{ch:te-evening}

\section[\te{సాయంత్రం}]{\te{సాయంత్రం} (sāyantram) — a distant cousin of French \textquotedblleft{}soir\textquotedblright{}}

\label{lesson:TE-C27-sayantram}



\begin{quote}
This lesson's word for \textquotedblleft{}evening\textquotedblright{} reaches back to a PIE root you've technically already met — in a completely different language, on a completely different continent's language family.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{సాయంత్రం}} (\textbf{sāyantram}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{evening}\textquotedblright{} — is a Sanskrit \textbf{tatsama}: from \textbf{\te{సాయం}} (\emph{sāyam}, \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{in the evening}\textquotedblright{}) plus a Sanskrit \textbf{-tana} suffix that turns time-adverbs into adjectives — the same suffix pattern behind Sanskrit \textbf{divātana} (\textquotedblleft{}of the day\textquotedblright{}) and \textbf{sanātana} (\textquotedblleft{}eternal, lasting\textquotedblright{}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{cousinweb}
Here's the striking part, checked directly against primary sources rather than assumed: \textbf{\te{సాయం}} itself traces to \textbf{Proto-Indo-European} \emph{\textbf{*seh\textsubscript{1}-}} (\textquotedblleft{}\textbf{long, lasting}\textquotedblright{}) — and this is \textbf{explicitly} documented as \textquotedblleft{}distantly related to \textbf{Latin sērus}\textquotedblright{} (\textquotedblleft{}late\textquotedblright{}), itself confirmed independently to trace to the very same \emph{*seh\textsubscript{1}-} root (via Proto-Italic \emph{*sēros}). You've technically already met \emph{sērus}: it's the Latin root already established in this course as the source of \textbf{French soir} and \textbf{Italian sera} — French and Italian's own everyday \textquotedblleft{}evening\textquotedblright{} words. That makes \textbf{\te{సాయంత్రం}} and \textbf{soir}/\textbf{sera} genuine distant cognates — one route through Sanskrit tatsama borrowing into Telugu, one route through centuries of Vulgar Latin erosion into French and Italian, both ultimately the same Proto-Indo-European idea of something \textquotedblleft{}long, lasting\textquotedblright{} stretching into \textquotedblleft{}late in the day.\textquotedblright{}
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}sāyantram\textquotedblright{} — \textquotedblleft{}evening,\textquotedblright{} sāyam + the -tana time-suffix
  \item the deep root — PIE \emph{seh\textsubscript{1}-, \textquotedblleft{}long, lasting\textquotedblright{}}
  \item the cross-family cognate — the same root behind French soir and Italian sera, via Latin sērus
\end{itemize}
